question.problem:
The data below is taken from the table of values of the cumulative distribution function $Φ(z)$ for the standard normal distribution. Given that $X∼N(\mu ,{3}^{2})$ is a normal random variable with $P(-0.7\mu <X<2.7\mu )=0.3256,$ find $\mu $ rounded to $2$ decimal places.

| $z$ | $\,0.01\,$ | $\,0.02\,$ | $\,0.03\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $\,0.3\,$ | $\,0.6217\,$ | $\,0.6255\,$ | $\,0.6293\,$ |
| $\,0.4\,$ | $\,0.6591\,$ | $\,0.6628\,$ | $\,0.6664\,$ |
| $\,0.5\,$ | $\,0.6950\,$ | $\,0.6985\,$ | $\,0.7019\,$ |

*Hint: Note that the interval $-0.7\mu <X<2.7\mu $ is symmetric about the mean $\mu .$*
question.worked_solution:
Note that we can write the given probability as

$$
P(\mu -1.7\mu <X<\mu +1.7\mu )=0.3256,
$$

which tells us that the interval $-0.7\mu <X<2.7\mu $ is symmetric about the mean $\mu .$

First, we find the cumulative probability using symmetry:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(\mu -1.7\mu <X<\mu +1.7\mu ) & =0.3256 \\ 2P(\mu <X<\mu +1.7\mu ) & =0.3256 \\ P(\mu <X<\mu +1.7\mu ) & =0.1628 \\ P(X<\mu +1.7\mu )-P(X<\mu ) & =0.1628 \\ P(X<\mu +1.7\mu )-0.5 & =0.1628 \\ P(X<\mu +1.7\mu ) & =0.6628 \\ P(X\le \mu +1.7\mu ) & =0.6628 \\ P(X\le 2.7\mu ) & =0.6628\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we transform to a standard normal random variable by $z$-scoring:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X\le 2.7\mu ) & =0.6628 \\ P(Z\le \frac{2.7\mu -\mu }{3}) & =0.6628 \\ Φ(\frac{1.7\mu }{3}) & =0.6628 \\ \frac{1.7\mu }{3} & ={Φ}^{-1}(0.6628)\end{aligned}
$$

According to the table, we have

$$
Φ(0.42)=0.6628\,⇒\,{Φ}^{-1}(0.6628)=0.42.
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1.7\mu }{3} & =0.42 \\ 1.7\mu  & =1.26 \\ \mu  & ≈0.741\,18 \\ \mu  & ≈0.74.\end{aligned}
$$
